title: Alexander’s conjecture on an inequality of Cassels
statement: For every integer $n\ge 1$, every real number $\rho>1$, and all complex numbers $z_1,\ldots,z_n$ satisfying $|z_j|\le \rho$ for $1\le j\le n$, prove that $\displaystyle\prod_{\substack{1\le j,k\le n\\ j\ne k}}\left|1-\overline{z_j}z_k\right|\le \left(\frac{\rho^{2n}-1}{\rho^2-1}\right)^n$.
references: - [A proof of Alexander’s Conjecture on an Inequality of Cassels](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11785-026-02048-7) — Complex Analysis and Operator Theory — Myriam Ounaïes

progress.label: Open · solution reported
progress.tldr: A new paper claims to prove the conjecture completely, but the result has not been independently verified here.
progress.summary:
Alexander’s conjecture concerns extending a product inequality of Cassels to all $\rho>1$. Myriam Ounaïes claims that the conjecture holds in full, with equality only for a regular $n$-gon on the boundary circle.

*[ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2601.10411) · [doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11785-026-02048-7)*

**Known results**

- Cassels proved the inequality under the restriction $\cos(\pi/n)\leq\rho^2/(\rho^4-\rho^2+1)$.
- Alexander observed that this restriction could be weakened to $\cos(\pi/n)\leq2\rho^2/(\rho^4+1)$ and conjectured validity for every $\rho>1$.
- Dubickas proved a related elementary-symmetric-function conjecture in degrees $1$ through $4$, which the paper says would imply Alexander’s conjecture.


**September 2026 proof claim**

Ounaïes’s preprint, also published in *Complex Analysis and Operator Theory*, claims the unrestricted inequality

$$\prod_{j\ne k}|1-\overline{z_j}z_k|\leq\left(\frac{\rho^{2n}-1}{\rho^2-1}\right)^n$$
\nfor $|z_j|\leq\rho$, with equality exactly at the vertices of a regular $n$-gon on $|z|=\rho$. The claim is unverified from the supplied evidence.



Current status (as of September 2026): Alexander’s conjecture is claimed solved by Ounaïes, but the proof and its exact publication scope remain independently unverified.

*Caveats. The retrieved publication record provides no abstract or theorem details, so the proof cannot be independently assessed from that record alone.*
